### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-shape.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-shape.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `34086270535c5be27c6daa03a8ac97ca0cf0781c` — the merge of head `35c4c3951de7696308d6ef6acc49a8eda6647100` into base `2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 34086270535c5be27c6daa03a8ac97ca0cf0781c && git checkout 34086270535c5be27c6daa03a8ac97ca0cf0781c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af 35c4c3951de7696308d6ef6acc49a8eda6647100 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af && git merge --no-ff 35c4c3951de7696308d6ef6acc49a8eda6647100

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2919ddb875cd0daa38ef452d741bcba04cf366af` → pass the list as

Local-runs: none

Reviewed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the narrowing face, as the dispatch asked: a security read-scope switch. Inputs: card #24932 (body and all 19 comments, including ruling B `6303721609`, ruling Q1 C / Q2 A `6329027469`, the dev reports `6318648840` and `6340537042`, the seat's decision `6340633145`, the ruling `6342223675`, engine seat 2's note `6309967905`, engine seat 1's pointer `6333147990`, the claims), the cross-lane declarations `6334266488` (#6367) and `6334275915` (#6017), the PR body, its file list, the net diff against `main` at this head (29 files, +1788 / −359; merge base `72a302a9d`, the dispatch base), and the head's check-runs. The cited engine code was read at this head (the PR does not touch it). Check-runs on the head: 40 success, 9 skipped, 0 failure; the five required contexts (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`) are all `success`, every Test Core shard included.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The four call sites answer the leaf — right.** `computeControlledByParentFilter` (`security-plugin.ts:8860`) is now synchronous and registry-only: `null` off a non-`controlled_by_parent` object, a system or user-less context, or a write verb; the deny sentinel by reference for an unresolvable relation; `{ fk: { $in: [] } }` for a cycle or over-depth chain; otherwise `{ fk: { $in: ReadableIds.of(rel.master) } }`. No up-front routing to an id list remains: the system-context `ql.find(rel.master, { fields: ['id'] })` scan is gone, and the three `fields: ['id']` reads left in the file (`:5927`, `:7600`, `:9753`) are the authored-row write probe, the #21829 predicate-write narrowing and the #25012 per-master collection, none of them the derivation. All four call sites take the leaf: the middleware's principal half (`:4488`) and delegator half (`:4507`), `getReadFilter` (`:6064`, with `'find'`) and `computeDelegatedReadFilter` (`:6179` and `:6181`, both legs). Row sets: the engine composes the leaf at its executor boundary (`engine.ts#composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`, `:6420`) from `canReadObject(master)` and `getReadFilter(master)` asked of this same plugin with the caller's context as it stands (`readableIdsScopeOf`, `:6640`), and the driver adds the tenant wall (D3). That is exactly the set the retired derivation composed by hand (object admission, RLS with tenant Layer 0, sharing, the master's own derivation), so the plain, restricted, unrestricted (`viewAllRecords`), null-FK, dangling-FK and master-object-unadmitted callers keep their rows by construction and by the real-stack pins in `controlled-by-parent-leaf-switch.test.ts` (SQLite and the PostgreSQL cell). The one row-set move is the fork-1 delegated row the ruling accepted: the engine asks `getReadFilter(master)` with the delegated context, which is `computeDelegatedReadFilter(master)`, the six layers the middleware composes for a delegated find of the master (principal RLS and leaf, delegator RLS and leaf, both sharing legs, the #25106 organization refusal mirrored), under `canReadObject(master)` for the same context. The detail's composed scope is therefore a subset of the master's delegated direct read, so no detail row is served that the caller cannot read on its master through a delegated direct read; the parity row (`d_under_theirs` 404 → 403, beside `p_theirs` already 403) and the chain row (`line_us` → `line_us, line_jp`, `line_own` still out) read as the pins say. The delegator half writes the same leaf, so a delegated read carries the subquery twice; the engine composes the master once and reuses it by reference, rows correct, as the ruling's execution parameter leaves it.

**(b) Cycle and over-depth — right, and the cut is the engine's.** `controlledByParentChainRefusal` (`:8925`) walks the registry alone (`getSchema`, `resolveCbpRelation`; no store work, no security call) before the leaf is written, and both guards answer `$in: []` with the error log naming the chain: zero rows, 200, never the engine's `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500. The cut: the plugin refuses when the read's object plus seven derived masters are followed by an eighth derived master (`chain.length` reaches `CBP_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` = 8 with the next master still derived); the engine refuses a ninth nested scope (`composeReadableIdsChain`, `ancestors.length` of 8 against `READABLE_IDS_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` = 8, `engine.ts:6510`). Both compose eight nested subqueries and refuse the ninth, so the plugin's walk pre-empts the engine's refusal on every declared chain, at every level (each master's own `getReadFilter` re-walks from itself). The real-stack pins hold it: a cycle and an over-depth chain answer zero rows with no `IN (SELECT` statement, and the eight-deep chain serves its row in one statement with eight nested subqueries. The two constants live in two packages and are equal by comment and by that real-stack pin, not by a shared export; the pin reddens on either moving, which is enough.

**(c) A write verb's predicate carries no leaf (ADR-0139 D1) — right; no caller-addressable write path loses the master check.** `CBP_LEAF_READ_VERBS` (`:562`) answers `null` for `update` / `delete`, and the engine itself refuses a leaf in a write's predicate at the executor's entry (`collectComposableReadableIds(object, 'update' | 'delete', …)`, `engine.ts:17659` and `:20890`), so the plugin could not have written one. The master check on the caller-addressable shapes: a by-id write is judged at the 2.8 gate (`assertControlledByParentWrite`, called at `:3276` and `:3286` for every write verb, not gated on the stand-down flags), which reads the row and walks the master chain; the predicate update or delete the caller addressed is narrowed to the rows the read door returns for the caller's own predicate (`readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite`, `:7585`, a `find` under the caller's context where the leaf composes) and judged per master by #25012 (`controlledByParentPredicateWriteMasters`). Deviation 3, accepted by ruling `6342223675` ③: the two #21829 stand-down shapes (`nestedInOperation`, `:2432`, a cascade or a hook's own write; `__referentialFieldClear`, `:2872`, the engine's integrity write) are excluded from the read narrowing by `addressedPredicateWrite` (`:7547`) and so now carry the RLS write filter only where they also carried `masterFK IN (readable master ids)`; the 2.8 gate still judges them per master over the rows the caller can read. Neither shape is addressed by a caller; the run-time measurement stays unmeasured, as the PR names.

**(d) Q2 A in `service-analytics` — right.** `admitReadableIds: true` is passed at exactly three sites, all engine-bound and all on the `scope` argument alone: `ObjectQLStrategy.withReadScope` (`:905`), `resolveFkAttr` (`:1430`) and the plugin's record-label pass (`plugin.ts:1081`, whose `$and` hands the scope to `executeAggregate`). `compileScopedFilterToSql` passes nothing and refuses a leaf-carrying scope first and by name (`findReadableIdsLeaf`, `read-scope-sql.ts:835`), in the withheld `READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED` / 500 envelope, which is the named echo deviation. `NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle` declines through `readScopeCarriesReadableIds` over the same object set the other content-based declines read (`readScopedObjects`, else the cube's base and declared joins), and `applyReadScope` compiles per object over that same set, so no compile site is reached that the decline did not see. An author's filter never meets the option: the caller's `where` goes through the engine's own door, the brand is a symbol key no JSON carries, and the three-faces suite pins the unbranded look-alike at `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 on every face with and without the leaf-carrying scope, the deny sentinel still serving nothing. The admission is for the scope `getReadScope` answers and nothing else.

**(e) Turso — right, nothing else moved.** `toRemoteWhere` (`turso-driver.ts:3400`) resolves a composed leaf's `scope` through itself with the outer read's `options`, so a nested composed leaf meets `replaceComposedReadableIds`, `remoteReadableIdsSemiJoin` and `remoteTenantScope` one level down and reaches the transport resolved; the only other change in the file is the docblock. The spec's new `READABLE_IDS_CASES` row measures the nested shape in every driver suite (the dev's ablation reddened it on the remote face alone).

**Public surface.** No metadata key, accepted value, export or default moves: `filter-comparand-shape.ts` changes a docblock sentence (not a `.describe()`), `readable-ids-conformance.ts` adds a fixture row, and `check:api-surface` / `check:docs` ran green inside the head's `TypeScript Type Check` job. The one visible runtime change is the `/analytics/sql` dry-run echo refusing for a `controlled_by_parent` object, loud and withheld, on a debugging aid, as ruling ⑤ names it.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` on the PR body and the changeset — right: the switch respells one existing scope, widens no accept set and adds no public name; the fork-1 row is a correction toward the master's own visibility that the ruling fixed as the contract, and the echo's refusal is a runtime answer on one shape of one debugging door, not a surface removal, so the `(narrowing)` arm is not owed. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: the spec docblock and the conformance row change no accept set or export. The level follows the kind: `patch` on all four moved packages (`plugin-security`, `service-analytics`, `driver-turso`, `spec`); `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The full dogfood battery is the dev's reading on this exact head under `os-verify-lock` (`6340537042`: 287 files passed / 3 skipped, 2395 tests passed / 18 skipped, 0 failures, command-exit 0), and the head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run is `success`; nothing was re-run here.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Two stale "one caller" sentences** (`packages/spec/src/data/readable-ids.ts:50-53`, `packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts:109`): confirmed stale at this head, prose only, outside the claim's bound (a second spec file, objectql). Escalated to the seat as a docs follow-up on the next PR touching either file; not a run-time claim and not a reason to hold this PR.
- **ADR-0139 D6's set-size-ceiling clause**: the accepted sentence is kept and the dated parenthetical beside it records the decision and points at ADR-0055's amendment and D5's note — no rewrite, which the maintainer re-read and approved in `6342223675`. Answered. One prose nit for a later Tier H edit, not for this one: the parenthetical dates ruling B as 2026-10-21 while its record stamp is 2026-10-20 (UTC), and dates the landing 2026-10-22 ahead of the merge.
- **ADR-0055**: every sentence the ruling names is corrected one by one — the status line (a new dated amendment line, the 2026-10-10 line left reading as of its date), `:74` set-size ceiling, `:75` per-request cost (twice per request, never cached), the amendment's `Read` paragraph and its `Cost` sentence — each as a dated note under the kept text. ADR-0139 D5's seventh-consumer note is worded "refuses at boot" with the late-registration limit, as engine seat 1's pointer asks.
- **The duplicated delegated subquery**: correct rows, one redundant subquery per delegated read; the ruling's execution parameter leaves it for a later simplification. Answered.
- **The cloud seat's staging read** (measurement condition 4): not this PR's; owed at the cloud seat's pin move after landing, as the ruling orders. Escalated there.
- **PG latency** (fork 2): accepted A by `6342223675` ②; no measurement card. Answered.
- **Deviation 3** (the two engine-internal write shapes): accepted as named; the run-time measurement is the seat's to ask for. Named above under (c).
- **Deviation 4** (PR on the dispatch base): 24 `main` commits since `72a302a9d`, none touching the PR's 29 files; one touches `engine.ts` (#25210, the tenancy ledger, away from the composition); the PR reads mergeable and clean, and the queue's merge-ref run validates the merge.
- **`readable-ids-in-memory.testkit.ts`** is a test double of the engine's five steps for the fake-engine suites; parity is pinned on the real stack in this package and in objectql. If the engine's composition moves, the testkit moves with it.
